title: Assessment lens (draft 0.2.0)
description: A set of criteria an assessment applies to a design specification. The core lens applies to every design; further lenses apply when a design declares, or is found to have, a profile. Each criterion says what it asks, why, what in the specification it reads, whether a tool can decide it or a reviewer must, how severe a failure is by default, and where it comes from. A criterion decided by tool or both may carry a declarative check, so an organisation's own criteria are machine-checked without code. Draft: see standards/assessment/standard-architecture-assessment.md.

prefix.description: The first part of every criterion id in the lens.

applies_when.description: always, the profile that brings the lens in, or the assessment trigger that does (the production lens applies to every production entry assessment).

reads.description: The parts of the design specification the criterion reads, as dotted paths.

decided_by.description: tool: decidable from the specification without judgement. reviewer: needs judgement. both: a tool decides whether the answer is present, a reviewer whether it is good enough.

rule.description: For a tool-decided criterion, the check in words precise enough to implement.

applies_to.description: When the criterion applies, if not always.

severity.description: The default severity of a not-met result. An assessor may change it with a reason.

check.description: A machine-checkable form of the rule: one rule or a list of rules over the design specification. Each rule picks items with for_each (a dotted path, stepping into every list on the way) and where, then requires fields of each, or counts them. Each required field of each item is a clause: every clause holding is met, some partly-met, none not-met, and nothing to check not-applicable. A shipped criterion is checked by code instead; a criterion with neither is reported as manual.

sources.description: Short source keys used by the criteria, each mapped to the full citation.

matcher.description: What the values at a field must be. A string, number or boolean means equals it; a list means each value is one of it. Over several values (a path through a list), equals, in and matches must hold for every value, and present for at least one.

conditions.description: Field path, relative to the item (. for the item itself), to matcher. All must hold.

for_each.description: Dotted path to the items checked, such as data or elements.agent.tools. Omitted, the rule checks the specification itself.

where.description: Only the items meeting these are checked.

require.description: What each chosen item must meet; each field is a clause.

count.description: Instead of require: how many items may match where. One clause.

message.description: The note when a clause fails. {id}, {name} or any field path of the item is filled in, and {field} with the required field.
